title: President's International Scholarship of Excellence
program_type: University merit entrance scholarship for international high-school applicants, requiring a separate application and a school nomination, with the value applied to the recipient's York Student Account
funding_type: Fixed-value university entrance scholarship ($45,000 CAD per year, published maximum $180,000 CAD over four years; university-funded)
administering_authority: York University — Student Recruitment & Admissions (Bennett Centre for Student Services) with Student Financial Services, Office of the University Registrar
implementing_agency: York University Student Recruitment & Admissions, which administers the International Student Scholarship & Award Application; the award is recorded in the official York University Award Search under the Office of the University Registrar
programme_action: York University 'Prestigious Scholarships' — President's International Scholarship of Excellence (PISE); cannot be held in conjunction with the York International Entrance Scholarship family (York International Scholarship of Distinction, York International Merit Award, York International Entrance Award, York International Transfer Award)
description: The President's International Scholarship of Excellence is York University's highest-value international entrance award, granted to international high-school applicants entering the first year of a four-year undergraduate degree who demonstrate academic excellence, commitment to volunteer work and extracurricular activities, and leadership skills. The published value is $180,000 CAD over four years ($45,000 per year), renewable for a further three years provided the recipient completes at least 24 credits in each Fall/Winter session with a minimum sessional GPA of 6.0. It is not automatic on admission: applicants must first apply for admission to York, obtain a York reference number, then complete the International Student Scholarship & Award Application and be nominated by a guidance counsellor, principal or senior school official, with a maximum of two nominations per school per year. York publishes no component breakdown of the $45,000 annual figure, so no claim is made here that it covers residence, meal plan or health insurance.

award_types: President's International Scholarship of Excellence (PISE) — separate application plus school nomination required
York International Scholarship of Distinction — automatic on admission, no application
York International Merit Award — automatic on admission, no application
York International Entrance Award — automatic on admission, no application
York International Transfer Award — automatic on admission, no application
Glendon International Excellence Scholarship — automatic on admission for Glendon admits, no application

award_types_detail.President's International Scholarship of: York's high-value international entrance scholarship, valued at $45,000 per year and published as $180,000 CAD over four years. A select number are awarded each year. Requires the International Student Scholarship & Award Application, a school nomination, a personal statement, a list of up to three extracurricular activities and community involvement entries, a list of up to three previous awards, and a financial profile. Not combinable with any entrance scholarship.
award_types_detail.York International Scholarship of Distin: Automatic entrance scholarship for international high-school applicants (including those with advanced standing under 24 transfer credits) with a final average of 90% or higher (85%+ on the page covering the 2025/26 cycle): $15,000 in year 1 and $7,500 in years 2, 3 and 4, to a maximum of $37,500. Renewable and regainable with 24 credits per year and a minimum 7.5 GPA (B+). York states that applicants admitted to Computer Science, Cybersecurity or Engineering are not eligible except for Fall 2026 international applicants completing high school under the Ontario curriculum.
award_types_detail.York International Merit Award: Automatic entrance scholarship for international high-school applicants (including advanced standing under 24 transfer credits) with a final average of 80%–89.9%: $10,000 in year 1 and $5,000 in years 2, 3 and 4, to a maximum of $25,000. Renewable and regainable with 24 credits per year and a minimum 7.5 GPA (B+).
award_types_detail.York International Entrance Award: Automatic one-time award of $5,000 for international high-school applicants or transfer students admitted with fewer than 24 transfer credits and a final average of 75%–79.9%.
award_types_detail.York International Transfer Award: Automatic one-time award of $2,500 for international transfer applicants admitted with 24 or more transfer credits and a minimum final average of 75%.
award_types_detail.Glendon International Excellence Scholar: Automatic scholarship of $10,000 per year ($40,000 over four years) for up to ten international students admitted to Glendon with top academic standing (80% or more, York Factor 8); renewable to a maximum of four years with a cumulative GPA of at least 8.0 over a minimum of 24 credits per school year.

programme_structure.renewal_criteria: York's official award database states the scholarship 'will be renewable for an additional three years of full-time study or until degree completion (whichever comes first) provided the recipient completes a minimum of 24 credits each Fall/Winter session with a minimum sessional grade point average of 6.0.' The incoming-students page words the same renewal more loosely as 'maintains good academic standing each year'. Renewal also requires accepted offer, satisfied admission conditions and full-time enrolment.
programme_structure.intake: Fall (September) entry. The PISE guides are written for the Fall 2027 intake and the application opens November 1, 2026; York also runs Winter (January) and Summer (May) intakes, for which the PISE guide is not published. York advises completing the admission application by January 19, 2027 so the York reference number is available before the scholarship deadline.

status_note: As at the 2026-10-10 verification date the 2026-entry cycle has closed and the 2027-entry cycle has not yet opened: York publishes 'The President's International Scholarship of Excellence Application opens November 1, 2026' and 'The International Scholarships and Awards application opens' on November 1, 2026. Published 2027-entry deadlines are January 27, 2027 (student application) and February 4, 2027 (nomination and reference letter), both in the future, so the status is UPCOMING rather than CLOSED. Next expected cycle: Fall 2028 entry, application opening late October or November 1, 2027.
verification_type: Direct verification from official futurestudents.yorku.ca and students.yorku.ca (yorku.ca) award, deadline, tuition and language pages, plus the official York University Award Search data file on students.yorku.ca and an authenticated asset check of the York University wordmark on the yorku.ca domain.
verification_notes: Eight official yorku.ca sources were read: the PISE award page, the PISE application guides page, the Scholarships and Awards for International Students page, the Scholarships/Awards/Bursaries for Incoming Students page, the Tuition & Fees page, the How Do I Apply page, the Undergraduate Language Proficiency Requirements page, and the official York University Award Search record (awardID 4849) together with its underlying award-search JSON. Deadline precision is exact. One inconsistency was found and resolved: the incoming-students page's PISE block prints 'Student Application Deadline: January 26, 2027' and also carries a stale 'January 26, 2026' sentence, whereas the PISE-specific page, the application-guides page and the international-scholarships page, plus the timeline section of the same incoming-students page, all state January 27, 2027; the cycle-specific PISE pages were treated as authoritative and January 27, 2027 recorded. Research was performed on 2026-10-10 (the retrieval date), superseding the SCHEMA_CONTRACT baseline date of 2026-10-03; this does not affect status because the January 27, 2027 deadline is in the future either way.
source_last_updated: The PISE application-guides page is refreshed for the Fall 2027 cycle (student deadline January 27, 2027; nomination deadline February 4, 2027; 'Application opens November 1, 2026'); the incoming-students page's PISE block still carries the prior-cycle January 26 date and a 'Fall/Winter 2026-2027' label; the tuition page states its figures are 2026-2027 estimates subject to change.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: Application opens November 1; student application due late January; nomination and reference letter due about eight days later in early February; admission decisions communicated in March; awards applied to the York Student Account in mid-August.
application_deadline.application_period: 2027 entry. The International Scholarships and Awards application opens November 1, 2026; applicants submit between November 2, 2026 and January 27, 2027; nominations must be submitted by February 4, 2027. York recommends submitting the admission application by January 19, 2027 so the York reference number is issued in time.
application_deadline.official_rule: The PISE page states 'Student Application Deadline: January 27, 2027' and the application-guides page states 'Student Application Deadline: January 27, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. EST' and 'Nomination & Reference Submission Deadline: February 4, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. EST'. The incoming-students page adds the rule that applications must be completed on the International Student Scholarship & Award Application 'by January 27, 2027 at 11:59:59 p.m. Eastern Time'. Because January in Toronto is Eastern Standard Time, 11:59 p.m. EST equals 2027-01-28T04:59:00Z.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: The nomination and reference-letter deadline (February 4, 2027) is separate from and later than the student deadline, but the student must enter the nominator's name, title and email in the application by January 27 for York to send the nomination link; a student who names a nominator late or whose school has used its two nomination slots cannot be considered. York also warns that a 9-digit York reference number is needed and is issued within about five business days of applying for admission, so applicants who apply for admission after roughly January 19, 2027 may not have a reference number before the scholarship deadline.

programme_duration.official_range: Four years of full-time undergraduate study; renewable for up to three additional years or until degree completion, whichever comes first
programme_duration.renewal_note: Renewable for three additional years of full-time study or to degree completion, whichever comes first, provided the recipient completes a minimum of 24 credits in each Fall/Winter session with a minimum sessional GPA of 6.0. York's incoming-students page also requires that recipients have accepted the offer by the offer-letter deadline, satisfied all admission conditions within 30 days of the start of term, and remain enrolled full-time.

funding.scholarship_type: Fixed-value university entrance scholarship (international merit award, university-funded)
funding.monthly_amount_note: York publishes no monthly stipend or living allowance for PISE. The only published value is an annual figure of $45,000 CAD per year.
funding.travel_amount_note: Travel to Canada is not named as a covered benefit on any official PISE page.
funding.institutional_costs: The award value is applied to the recipient's York Student Account against tuition and other student fees. York's 2026-2027 approximate international tuition is $40,000 for most Arts and Science programs, $40,000-$44,000 for Business, $38,000 for Computer Science, $40,000 for Design and $47,000 for Engineering, so $45,000 per year is on the scale of one year of international tuition for most programs but not for Engineering. York does not publish a fixed allocation of the award between tuition and other charges.
funding.fully_funded_note: Not fully funded in the published sense. York does not state that PISE covers the full cost of attendance, does not list residence, meal plan or health insurance as award benefits, states that 'Scholarships and awards for international students are limited and you should be prepared to support yourself throughout your studies at York', requires all undergraduate international students to pay a $2,000 non-refundable acceptance deposit regardless of scholarship status, and states of the parallel 4-year residence guarantee that it 'is not part of any financial commitment from York. Students will still need to pay for residence and meal plans.' What is published is an annual value of $45,000 CAD applied to the student account.

tuition.conditions: Published annual value, applied to the recipient's York Student Account against tuition and other student fees. York does not publish a component breakdown, so this line records the annual value as published rather than a stated tuition-only entitlement. The official award database records the value as 'Up to 45000', so the annual figure is a maximum.

monthly_stipend.note: Not published in official source. York publishes no stipend or living allowance for PISE.

visa_support.note: Not published in official source. Study-permit guidance is published separately by York International.

insurance.note: Not published as an award benefit. York's tuition page lists health and dental care at $359 for domestic students and $1,151 for international students, including the University Health Insurance Plan (UHIP) and the YFS/Glendon plan; these remain student budget items.

accommodation_support.note: York does not publish residence or meal-plan coverage as part of PISE. Direct-entry international students starting at York in Fall 2025, Winter 2026, Fall 2026 or Fall 2027 receive a 4-year on-campus housing/residence guarantee, but York states this guarantee 'is not part of any financial commitment from York. Students will still need to pay for residence and meal plans.' Published 2026-2027 residence cost estimates are $9,000-$13,000 for residence/apartment (8-month rates) and $4,350-$8,000 for meal plans.

bond.note: No service bond, repayment obligation or return-of-funds condition is published. The continuing conditions are full-time enrolment, the renewal credit and GPA requirement, and adjustment of the award value to domestic tuition fee values if the recipient's immigration status changes to an exempt category.

total_estimated_value.note: York publishes the headline figure as '$180,000 CAD valued over four years ($45,000/year)' on the PISE and international-scholarships pages, while the official award database records the value as 'Up to 45000' and York's international scholarship awareness page says 'up to $180,000 CAD'. The 'up to' wording means the four-year total is an upper bound rather than a guaranteed entitlement, so no separately computed total is asserted here.

Value applied to the recipient's York Student Account against tuition and other student fees
Renewal for up to three additional years, or to degree completion, whichever comes first, subject to at least 24 credits per Fall/Winter session and a minimum 6.0 sessional GPA

Automatic consideration for other international entrance scholarships, including the Liberal Arts & Professional Studies International Undergraduate Leadership Scholarship where applicable, if the applicant is not selected for PISE

Non-monetary President's International Scholars benefits published by York: complimentary registration at York's annual Career Ready Conference in every year of study, mentor matching from day one, and faculty networking engagement with senior leaders and professors

Recipient testimonials on the PISE page describe the award — in one case combined with the International Entrance Scholarship — as covering tuition, living expenses, accommodation, health plan and meal plan; these are personal statements by named students, not York's published benefit structure, and are not recorded as coverage

eligible_applicants: High-school students entering the first year of a four-year undergraduate degree program at York University in the entry term (Fall 2027 for the current cycle)
Applicants who hold international student status and are subject to international tuition fees throughout their studies at York
Applicants with strong academic performance, including a minimum final admission average of 80% (A) or equivalent
Applicants demonstrating leadership skills and active involvement in volunteer work and extracurricular activities
Applicants officially nominated by a guidance counsellor, principal or senior school official, with a maximum of two nominations per school per year
Applicants who have applied for admission to a York undergraduate program and hold a 9-digit York reference number
final_year_condition: PISE is an entrance award for the first year of a four-year undergraduate degree, so final-year high-school students are the intended applicants rather than final-year bachelor's students. The eligibility bullet requires the applicant to be a high-school student entering the first year of an undergraduate degree at York in the entry term; York's incoming-students definition of a high-school applicant also requires that the applicant be less than 21 years old by December 31 of the admission year, out of full-time high school for less than two years, and have not attempted studies at an accredited college or university.
equivalent_degree_note: Yes. The eligibility requirement is expressed as a minimum final admission average of 80% (A) 'or equivalent', and York's award database states 'A minimum 'A' average or equivalent (York factor 8 or 9) is required to be considered'. Equivalence is determined by the applicant's curriculum and grading scale; York states on the international-scholarships page that 'Your school's grading system may not be equivalent to York's grading scale.'

age_limit.age_calculation_date: Applicant must be less than 21 years old by December 31 of the calendar year of admission (applicants admitted for a Fall term must be less than 21 by December 31 of that year)

eligibility.citizenship: No nationality restriction. York states that recipients 'will represent a variety of regions around the world', and the official award database records the award's status as 'International Student'. The binding condition is international fee status rather than nationality.
eligibility.residence_requirement: The applicant must hold international student status and be subject to international tuition fees during their studies at York. If the recipient's immigration status changes to an exempt category, the award value is adjusted to reflect domestic tuition fee values, and York reserves the right to revoke or discontinue an international entrance scholarship if the recipient's tuition category changes to domestic.
eligibility.age_limit: York's definition of a high-school applicant, published on the incoming-students page, requires the applicant to be less than 21 years old by December 31 of the calendar year of admission, out of full-time high school studies for less than two years from the graduation date, and not to have attempted studies at an accredited college or university. The PISE eligibility bullets themselves state only that the applicant must be a high-school student entering the first year of an undergraduate degree.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Must be a high-school student entering the first year of a four-year undergraduate degree at York in the entry term (Fall 2027 for the current cycle), and must be nominated by a guidance counsellor, principal or senior school official at the current high school; a maximum of two nominations per school per year are accepted.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Minimum final admission average of 80% (A) or equivalent for consideration; the official award database states a minimum 'A' average or equivalent (York factor 8 or 9). This is an eligibility floor, not a guarantee of selection.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Renewal requires a minimum of 24 credits completed in each Fall/Winter session with a minimum sessional GPA of 6.0. (The parallel automatic international entrance scholarships use a 7.5 GPA / B+ over 24 credits for their renewal.)
eligibility.language_requirement: An English or French language proficiency requirement applies to admission at York and is not a PISE-specific rule. Programs at Keele Campus are taught in English and Glendon Campus programs in a bilingual English/French environment, so applicants must demonstrate proficiency in their program's language of instruction. General York minimums for applicants required to submit a test: TOEFL iBT 88 for tests taken before January 2026 or 4.5 on the new scale for tests taken from January 2026; IELTS Academic 6.5; PTE Academic 60; CAEL 60; Cambridge C1 Advanced with no score below 180; Duolingo 120. Tests are valid for two years. Higher program-specific minimums apply for Nursing (IELTS 7.0 / TOEFL iBT 94 or 5.0 / PTE 67 / Duolingo 130 / C1 Advanced 193 / CAEL 67), Schulich School of Business (IELTS 7.0 / TOEFL iBT 94 or 5.0 / PTE 67 / Duolingo 130 / C1 Advanced 193 / CAEL 67) and Lassonde Engineering (IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0, TOEFL iBT 88 or 4.5 with section minimums, PTE 60, Duolingo 120 with no section below 105).
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: Required as part of the profile: applicants must demonstrate 'active involvement in volunteer work and extracurricular activities', and the application requires a list of Extracurricular Activities & Community Involvement of at most three entries.
eligibility.financial_need: Financial need is not an eligibility requirement, but the application requires 'a financial profile indicating the estimated total amount of funding you will have to support your studies over the next three to four years', and the official award database states that 'Financial need may also be considered in the selection process.'
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: PISE cannot be held in conjunction with the York International Scholarship of Distinction, the York International Merit Award, the York International Entrance Award or the York International Transfer Award; York states that students may apply for its prestigious scholarships and, if successful, will receive the higher-value award. The official award database additionally states that the scholarship cannot be held in conjunction with the York University Continuing Student Scholarship.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Must be entering the first year of a four-year undergraduate degree program, hold a 9-digit York reference number from an application for admission for the relevant term, and remain enrolled full-time in a York undergraduate program. Recipients must have accepted the offer of admission by the deadline in the offer letter and satisfied all outstanding admission conditions within 30 days of the start of the term.
eligibility.field_restrictions: None for PISE. The award is open to applicants across York's faculties; 2025 President's International Scholars are listed from the Schulich School of Business, Glendon College, the Faculty of Environmental & Urban Change, the Faculty of Health, the Faculty of Science, the School of the Arts, Media, Performance & Design, the Faculty of Liberal Arts & Professional Studies and the Lassonde School of Engineering. Field restrictions apply only to the parallel automatic awards (for example, applicants admitted to Computer Science, Cybersecurity or Engineering are excluded from the York International Scholarship of Distinction except for Fall 2026 Ontario-curriculum high-school applicants).

academic_requirements.fixed_percentage_requirement: Minimum final admission average of 80% (A) or equivalent
academic_requirements.percentage_note: The PISE page requires 'a minimum final admission average of 80% (A) or equivalent'; the official award database requires 'A minimum 'A' average or equivalent (York factor 8 or 9)'. The 80% figure is a floor for consideration, not a guarantee of selection, and is assessed against the applicant's curriculum and grading scale.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: No program-specific academic requirement is published for PISE. Supp entry programs have separate supplementary applications and deadlines (Schulich BBA February 1, 2027; AMPD evaluation February 5, 2027; Creative Writing February 5, 2027; Concurrent Education March 19, 2027; Glendon International Studies & Business Administration dual degree March 31, 2027), but these are admission requirements and do not condition PISE eligibility.
selection_factors_may_include: Exceptional academic profile and final admission average
Commitment to volunteer work and community service
Active involvement in extracurricular activities, including excellence in the arts or sport
Previous awards (at most three listed in the application)
Financial need, which York's award database states 'may also be considered in the selection process'
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: York describes the award as recognising applicants with 'an exceptional academic profile, and who demonstrate leadership through community service or excellence in the arts or sport', alongside academic excellence, volunteer work, extracurricular activities and leadership skills. York publishes no numeric weighting, rubric or scoring methodology.

english_requirement.moi_rule: Applicants are not required to submit proof of English proficiency if they have completed, or are completing, four full years of study in English (or French) at an accredited high school in Canada or where English is the official primary language of the country; four full years of high-school study where English is the primary language of instruction; one full year of study in an accredited English-medium university degree program; or two full years of study in an accredited English-medium college diploma or applied degree program. Waivers may also apply for IB Diploma or IB Career-related Programme study in English or French, GCE/GCSE/IGCSE English at Ordinary level grade B (6 in reformed qualifications) or predicted A/AS/AICE level C, CSEC/CAPE studies, AP College Board examinations at an English-medium school, and four years of English-medium study through the CBSE or CISCE boards. Time spent in ESL courses does not count, and requirements are not waived on the basis of letters, SAT/ACT scores or senior high-school English courses.
english_requirement.test_score_note: These are York's general undergraduate admission minimums, not PISE-specific scores, and meeting them does not guarantee admission. York states it reserves the right to require a successfully completed language proficiency test. Accepted tests and minimums: TOEFL iBT 88 for tests taken before January 2026 and 4.5 for tests taken from January 2026 onwards (York institution code 0894); IELTS Academic 6.5 (IELTS General is not accepted; TOEFL iBT Home Edition and IELTS One Skill Retake are accepted if minimums are met); PTE Academic 60; CAEL 60; Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE/CPE) with no score below 180; Duolingo 120. Higher program-specific minimums apply for Nursing, Schulich School of Business and Lassonde Engineering. Tests are valid for two years. Results must be sent by the test centre to York (IELTS/TOEFL electronically to institution 0894; CAEL, Cambridge and Duolingo via the applicant's account; PTE by emailing the Score Report Code to study@yorku.ca). Uploading scores to MyFile is not permitted.
accepted_tests: TOEFL iBT (including TOEFL iBT Home Edition)

language_of_instruction.language_note: Programs at Keele Campus are offered in English, while programs at Glendon Campus are offered in a bilingual English/French environment. Applicants must demonstrate proficiency in their program's language of instruction; Glendon publishes its own approved French language test list. Applicants below the English standard may enter through York University English Language Institute (YUELI) pathway programs, including Integrated Year One, Accelerated English and Academic Credit English.

application_method.application_route: Apply for admission to a York University undergraduate program for the entry term (through the Ontario Universities' Application Centre or the York University application), receive the 9-digit York reference number, then complete the International Student Scholarship & Award Application online using that reference number, and ensure the nominating school official submits the official nomination form and reference letter by February 4, 2027.
application_steps: 1. Confirm eligibility: high-school student entering the first year of an undergraduate degree at York in the entry term; international student status subject to international tuition fees; strong academic performance, leadership skills and active involvement in volunteer work and extracurricular activities; minimum final admission average of 80% (A) or equivalent.
2. Secure an official nomination from a guidance counsellor, principal or senior school official. A maximum of two nominations per school per year are accepted.

3. Apply for admission to a York University undergraduate program for the entry term through OUAC or the York University application. For Fall 2027 entry the international applicant deadline is March 24, 2027, but York recommends applying by January 19, 2027 so the York reference number is issued before the scholarship deadline.

4. Receive the 9-digit York reference number (issued within about five business days of the admission application) and use it to log in to the International Student Scholarship & Award Application, which opens November 1, 2026.

5. Complete the online application: a personal statement of at most 500 words on personal professional goals, leadership skills and commitment to volunteer work and extracurricular activities; a list of Extracurricular Activities & Community Involvement (maximum of three); a list of Previous Awards (maximum of three); the nominator's contact details; a financial profile indicating the estimated total funding available for the next three to four years; and optionally an additional reference letter highlighting community involvement.
6. Submit the application by January 27, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. EST.

7. Ensure the nominator completes the official nomination form and submits the signed reference letter on school letterhead, following the link York emails after submission, by February 4, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. EST.

8. Await notification: award decisions for incoming students are communicated by email in March 2027, and awards are applied to the York Student Account and reflected on the August statement (mid-August 2027).
application_method.application_fee: No separate scholarship application fee is published. All undergraduate international students must pay York's $2,000 non-refundable acceptance deposit regardless of scholarship status; the admission application fee is separate.

degree_outcome.degree_note: PISE funds a first undergraduate degree at York University across all faculties; 2025 President's International Scholars are listed from Schulich, Glendon, Environmental & Urban Change, Health, Science, the School of the Arts, Media, Performance & Design, Liberal Arts & Professional Studies and Lassonde. Entrance scholarship and residence-guarantee offers expire with the acceptance deadline indicated in offer letters, and scholarship offers are automatically deferred for applicants who defer admission to Winter 2027; deferring beyond the 2026-2027 academic year subjects the applicant to the scholarship program in effect at the new point of admission.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: PISE requires entry as a high-school student into the first year of a four-year undergraduate degree, so no advanced-standing credit is contemplated for the award itself. York's automatic international awards do consider transfer applicants: the York International Scholarship of Distinction and Merit Award cover applicants with advanced standing of fewer than 24 transfer credits, while the York International Transfer Award requires 24 or more transfer credits.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Recipients are students paying international tuition fees. The award value is applied to the recipient's York Student Account against tuition and other student fees. International entrance scholarships are applicable only to students paying international tuition rates, and York reserves the right to revoke or discontinue the scholarship if the recipient's tuition category changes to domestic; the official award database states the value will be adjusted to reflect domestic tuition fee values if the recipient's immigration status changes and they are exempted from paying international fees.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: No scholarship application fee is published. All undergraduate international students are required to pay the $2,000 non-refundable acceptance deposit regardless of scholarship status.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: To maintain scholarship eligibility, students must have accepted their offer of admission by the deadline indicated in their offer letter, have satisfied all outstanding admission conditions within 30 days of the start of the applicable term, and be enrolled full-time in a York University undergraduate program. Scholarship offers are automatically deferred for applicants who defer admission to Winter 2027; those who defer beyond the 2026-2027 academic year are subject to the scholarship program in effect at the new point of admission.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: President's International Scholars receive complimentary registration for York's annual Career Ready Conference in every year of study, mentor matching from day one, and faculty networking engagement with senior leaders and professors. Direct-entry international students starting at York in Fall 2027 also receive a 4-year on-campus housing/residence guarantee, which York states is not a financial commitment and still requires payment of residence and meal plans. Standard services include York International support, immigration advising and UHIP health insurance.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: No bond or repayment obligation is published. Loss or reduction of the award arises from the recipient's tuition category changing to domestic (value adjusted to domestic fee values), failure to meet the renewal requirement of 24 credits per Fall/Winter session with a minimum 6.0 sessional GPA, failure to maintain full-time enrolment, or deferring admission beyond the 2026-2027 academic year.

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: Use the 500-word personal statement to give concrete evidence for each of York's three stated pillars — academic excellence, volunteer work and extracurricular activities, and leadership. Name the initiative, your specific role, what changed and who benefited, rather than asserting qualities. State professional goals explicitly, since York asks the statement to speak to 'your personal professional goals'. Because a guidance counsellor or senior school official must confirm the nomination and write the reference letter on school letterhead, give that person the same evidence base so the letter can corroborate your claims about academic achievement, extracurricular involvement and community contribution.

database_notes: No substitution was required. The assigned target — York University's President's International Scholarship of Excellence (PISE) and its International Entrance Scholarship family for international undergraduates — is not on the DO-NOT-DUPLICATE list, Canada is an allowed region, and the award funds a first bachelor's degree. No existing record in research/bachelor covers York University or PISE.

The record is written for PISE as the named target, with the York International Entrance Scholarship family (York International Scholarship of Distinction, York International Merit Award, York International Entrance Award, York International Transfer Award, plus the Glendon International Excellence Scholarship) recorded in programme_structure.award_types and degree_outcome.possible_awards, because York's official pages present them as the mutually exclusive alternative: PISE 'cannot be held in conjunction with' these entrance scholarships, and a student who applies for York's prestigious scholarships receives the higher-value award if successful. Applicants who are not selected for PISE are automatically considered for other international entrance scholarships.

Coverage precision (the key accuracy question): York publishes only a value — '$180,000 CAD valued over four years ($45,000/year)' — and records it as 'Up to 45000' in the official award database. No official yorku.ca page states that the $45,000 per year covers residence, meal plan or health insurance, and York explicitly states that the 4-year residence guarantee 'is not part of any financial commitment from York. Students will still need to pay for residence and meal plans', that all international undergraduates pay a $2,000 non-refundable acceptance deposit regardless of scholarship status, and that international students 'should be prepared to support yourself throughout your studies at York'. The award value is applied to the recipient's York Student Account against tuition and other student fees. Recipient testimonials on the PISE page describe broader coverage (tuition, living expenses, accommodation, health plan, meal plan), in one case combined with the International Entrance Scholarship; these are personal statements and are deliberately not recorded as coverage.

fully_funded is set to false. Although $45,000 per year exceeds York's published 2026-2027 international tuition estimate for most programs ($40,000 Arts and Science, $40,000-$44,000 Business, $38,000 Computer Science, $40,000 Design, $47,000 Engineering), York publishes no statement that PISE covers the full cost of attendance, and several costs are explicitly excluded by York's own wording.

Deadline precision is 'exact': the PISE application-guides page publishes 'Student Application Deadline: January 27, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. EST' and 'Nomination & Reference Submission Deadline: February 4, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. EST', and the incoming-students page requires the application 'by January 27, 2027 at 11:59:59 p.m. Eastern Time'. The timezone is recorded as America/Toronto (Eastern Standard Time, UTC-05:00) because January in Toronto is EST; 11:59 p.m. EST equals 2027-01-28T04:59:00Z.

An internal inconsistency was found and resolved: the incoming-students page's PISE block prints 'Student Application Deadline: January 26, 2027' and also carries the sentence 'well in advance of the scholarship application deadline January 26, 2026'. January 26, 2026 was the deadline of the previous (Fall 2026) cycle. Two cycle-specific pages and the timeline section of the incoming-students page all state January 27, 2027, so January 27, 2027 was recorded as the deadline; the stray January 26, 2027 date is flagged in verification_notes and in risk_flags.

single_central_deadline is false because the cycle has two sequential deadlines (student application January 27, 2027; nomination and reference letter February 4, 2027), and because the admission application must precede them.

status is UPCOMING rather than OPEN: at the verification date York states 'The President's International Scholarship of Excellence Application opens November 1, 2026' and 'The International Scholarships and Awards application opens' on November 1, 2026, so the window has not yet opened, while both 2027-entry deadlines are in the future. It is not CLOSED because the deadline is later than the verification date.

age_limit is populated from York's generic high-school-applicant definition on the incoming-students page (less than 21 years old by December 31 of the admission calendar year, out of full-time high school for under two years, no prior college or university study) rather than from a PISE-specific rule; the PISE eligibility bullets state only that the applicant must be a high-school student entering the first year of an undergraduate degree. maximum_age is recorded as 20 because the rule is 'less than 21'.

english_requirement records York's general undergraduate admission minimums (IELTS Academic 6.5, TOEFL iBT 88 pre-January 2026 or 4.5 from January 2026, PTE Academic 60, CAEL 60, Cambridge C1 Advanced 180, Duolingo 120; validity two years) with program-specific higher minimums for Nursing, Schulich and Lassonde. These are admission requirements, not PISE-specific scholarship criteria, and York states that meeting minimums does not guarantee admission. The TOEFL dual-scale entry reflects York's own published table.

previous_emjm_scholarship_ineligible is false, as required for a bachelor's award. The applicable restriction — that PISE cannot be held with the automatic international entrance scholarships or the York University Continuing Student Scholarship — is recorded in eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction, because the schema forbids an extra top-level key for it.

The official award terms are published in the York University Award Search record (awardID 4849) at https://students.yorku.ca/sfs/scholarships-awards-bursaries?awardID=4849, recorded here as official_catalogue_url.

'PISE' is the short form used by York itself on the official pages, so short_title is an official acronym rather than a convenience abbreviation. legacy_titles is empty: 'President's International Scholars' is the recipient designation used by York, not a former name of the award.
